It stays usable -\n   * the record is advice, never a trust decision - but the row has to say so,\n   * because it otherwise looks exactly like a table that works.\n   */\n  tableMarkedNotWorking?: string | null;\n  /**\n   * What is known about the table this game is actually on, as the same glyph\n   * Manage and Search use.\n   *\n   * It was the one table with no mark anywhere on the panel: the row said\n   * \"marked as not working\" in words and said nothing at all about a table that\n   * had been proven to work, so the state of the table a user is using was the\n   * one state they had to open another screen to see.\n   */\n  tableEvidence?: CompatibilityEvidence;\n  tableBlocked?: BlockedMark | null;\n  onOpenImportedTables: () => void;\n  runtimeReady: boolean;\n  runtimeText: string;\n  /**\n   * `runtimeText` says a short complete fact and can be read where it is.\n   *\n   * The row truncates, and a truncated row with no focus stop cannot be opened\n   * by any controller press, so the reason a session failed or recovered has to\n   * keep its stop. Decided where the text is, because only that branch knows\n   * whether the line carries a backend message or a Windows process name.\n   */\n  runtimeTextComplete: boolean;\n  /**\n   * The cause for the runtime row's label, where the backend named a short one.\n   *\n   * Both halves of a cut row are cut, so this is about order rather than about\n   * space: the label is read first and shown first, and a row that spends it on\n   * `Table not loaded` says only what the row already means. Absent, the row\n   * keeps that generic label, which is still the right one when the backend\n   * named no cause or named one too long to lead with.\n   */\n  runtimeLabel?: string;\n  /** The table exceeds the live-control budget, so no snapshot is possible. */\n  liveControlsUnavailable: boolean;\n  /** The bridge is attached but never got this table into Cheat Engine. */\n  tableLoadFailed?: boolean;\n  /** Why the last live-state read failed, when one did. The session itself is\n      unaffected: reading the live state is not what makes a launch succeed. */\n  liveSnapshotError: string | null;\n  /** Start CE for the table this profile already authorized, without re-importing it. */\n  startRuntimeAvailable: boolean;\n  startRuntimeBlockedReason: string | null;\n  onStartRuntime: () => void;\n  activeCheatLabels: string[];\n  activeCheatSnapshotReady: boolean;\n  /**\n   * Enclosing scripts and attach-only records that are on.\n   *\n   * Counted apart from the cheats because they are not choices: CE Decky\n   * switches them on itself to reach the cheat that needs them, and the picker\n   * lists them apart for the same reason. Said rather than hidden, because a\n   * user who switched one cheat on and is told two things are running should be\n   * able to see where the second came from.\n   */\n  activeScriptCount: number;\n  pinnedCount: number;\n  /** Pinned cheats the running table does not have, so no row can be drawn for them. */\n  pinnedMissing?: number;\n  /** Pinned controls promoted onto this panel, with their live active state. */\n  pinnedRows: PinnedCheatRow[];\n  pinnedBusyRecordId: number | null;\n  onTogglePinnedCheat: (recordId: number, active: boolean) => void;\n  onChooseCheats: () => void;\n  /** Switch off every active control without stopping Cheat Engine. */\n  onDisableAllCheats: () => void;\n  autoloadEnabled: boolean;\n  /** Why auto-load cannot be changed right now, or `null` when it can. */\n  autoloadBlockedReason: string | null;\n  onAutoloadChange: (enabled: boolean) => void;\n  ceRunning: boolean;\n  /** Why the global Cheat Engine identity cannot be changed, or `null`. */\n  ceIdentityBlockedReason: string | null;\n  /** A launch that has started and is still waiting for the resident bridge. */\n  launchPending: boolean;\n  onStopCE: () => void;\n  /** Why no table may be started in this game until it is restarted, where the backend holds it. */\n  dirtyRunNotice?: string | null;\n  onClearDirtyRun?: () => void;\n  onAdvanced: () => void;\n  busy: boolean;\n  error: string | null;\n}\n\n/**\n * The compact CE Decky quick-access panel.\n *\n * Everything above the cheats is context a user reads once and changes rarely,\n * so Cheat Engine, the current game and the selected table are one row each and\n * carry their own small action instead of a full-width button. The cheats\n * themselves - the reason the panel exists - keep the full-width controls and\n * must be reachable without scrolling the quick-access column.\n */\nexport function HomePanel(props: Props) {\n  const {\n    pluginVersion,\n    updateVersion,\n    onUpdate,\n    mascotVisible,\n    updateRunning,\n    ceReady,\n    ceStatusText,\n    installAvailable,\n    installBusy,\n    managedCancelling = false,\n    setupPending,\n    setupStatusError,\n    onRetrySetupStatus,\n    installOperation,\n    ceSource,\n    ceSha256,\n    onInstall,\n    onCancelInstall,\n    reinstallLabel,\n    onReinstall,\n    game,\n    appDetails,\n    runningDetectionAvailable,\n    runningGameCount,\n    selectedGameRunning = false,\n    targetProcess,\n    targetNotRunning = null,\n    onChooseGame,\n    table,\n    tableSource,\n    onSearchTable,\n    searchButtonRef,\n    preferSearchFocus = false,\n    selectedTableMissing = null,\n    tableMarkedNotWorking = null,\n    tableEvidence,\n    tableBlocked = null,\n    onOpenImportedTables,\n    runtimeReady,\n    runtimeText,\n    runtimeTextComplete,\n    runtimeLabel,\n    liveControlsUnavailable,\n    tableLoadFailed,\n    liveSnapshotError,\n    startRuntimeAvailable,\n    startRuntimeBlockedReason,\n    onStartRuntime,\n    activeCheatLabels,\n    activeCheatSnapshotReady,\n    activeScriptCount,\n    pinnedCount,\n    pinnedMissing = 0,\n    pinnedRows,\n    pinnedBusyRecordId,\n    onTogglePinnedCheat,\n    onChooseCheats,\n    onDisableAllCheats,\n    autoloadEnabled,\n    autoloadBlockedReason,\n    onAutoloadChange,\n    ceRunning,\n    ceIdentityBlockedReason,\n    launchPending,\n    onStopCE,\n    dirtyRunNotice = null,\n    onClearDirtyRun = () => undefined,\n    onAdvanced,\n    busy,\n    error,\n  } = props;\n  const workflowBlocked = busy || setupPending || updateRunning;\n  const searchDisabled = workflowBlocked || !game;\n  // See `preferSearchFocus`: the mount decides, and nothing after it does.\n  //\n  // Only where Search can take it. A disabled control refuses the initial focus\n  // and Advanced has been told not to ask for it, which is a panel opening with\n  // nothing asking at all; the panel moves the ring itself once the control can\n  // be pressed, and until then Advanced is where a panel opens.\n  const openOnSearch = useRef(preferSearchFocus && !searchDisabled).current;\n  // A table past the live-control budget has no snapshot and never will, so the\n  // runtime row must not point at Configure cheats - the one screen that\n  // refuses a table this size. The session itself is fine.\n  // A session that never got its table has nothing to refresh, so the hint\n  // about opening Configure cheats would be advice to press a button that can\n  // only report the same emptiness. The runtime row says what happened instead.\n  // The hint, and whether the reader can finish it where it stands, decided the\n  // same way the line under it is: copy this frontend wrote is known and wraps,\n  // while a message the backend wrote has no bounded length and keeps a stop\n  // rather than pushing the panel's controls down the screen.\n  const liveStateHint = liveControlsUnavailable\n    ? {\n      text: \"Live controls are unavailable for a table this size. Cheats saved for this table still load automatically.\",\n      complete: true,\n    }\n    // A failed read of the live state says so instead of implying the session\n    // is fine and the user simply has not looked yet. Cheat Engine is attached\n    // either way, so this never contradicts a successful launch.\n    : liveSnapshotError\n      ? {\n        text: leadWithCause(liveSnapshotError, \"The live cheat state could not be read; open Configure cheats to try again.\"),\n        complete: false,\n      }\n      : { text: \"Open Configure cheats to refresh the live state.\", complete: true };\n  // The runtime row carries a hint only while a connected session cannot be\n  // read; the rest of the time it repeats state the row's own label already\n  // gives.\n  const runtimeHint = runtimeReady && !activeCheatSnapshotReady && !tableLoadFailed ? liveStateHint : null;\n  // What is on, counted as the user chose it. A table's own scripts are on\n  // because a cheat needed them, so they are named as what they are instead of\n  // being added to a number that is meant to match the switches on this panel.\n  const activeCheatSummary = activeCountLabel(activeCheatLabels.length, activeScriptCount);\n  // Read in place unless whichever of the two is on the row was written\n  // somewhere this frontend cannot see the length of.\n  const runtimeRowStatus = launchPending || (runtimeHint === null ? runtimeTextComplete : runtimeHint.complete);\n  const ceDetail = [ceSource, ceSha256 ? ceSha256.slice(0, 8) : null, pluginVersion]\n    .filter(Boolean).join(\" · \");\n  // Changing the game underneath a running one is a press away from every\n  // question this plugin answers per game: which table is prepared, which\n  // process is the target, which session an owned Cheat Engine holds. The panel\n  // says nothing about it - a running game is the ordinary state, and a line\n  // explaining a press nobody made costs a row of a 300 pixel column every\n  // session - so `README.md` carries it under **Pick the game** instead.\n\n  // Whether the row under the start press is about to say why it cannot be\n  // pressed. A target this game is not running is one of those reasons, and it\n  // is said there in full - what the game did start, and where the setting\n  // lives - so its own row above stands only where that row does not: while\n  // Cheat Engine is connected, while a launch is running, and behind a refusal\n  // that outranks it, which is what an anti-cheat is.\n  const startBlockedRowShown = Boolean(\n    table && !runtimeReady && !launchPending && !startRuntimeAvailable && startRuntimeBlockedReason,\n  );\n  const gameChangeBlocked = Boolean(game) && selectedGameRunning;\n  const gameDetail = game\n    ? [game.isShortcut ? \"Non-Steam\" : \"Steam\", targetProcess || `AppID ${game.appId}`].join(\" · \")\n    : runningDetectionAvailable\n      ? runningGameCount > 1 ? `${runningGameCount} games running; choose one` : \"Start a game or choose one\"\n      : \"Automatic detection is unavailable; choose one\";\n\n  return (\n    <DensePanel>\n      {/* HexPaw sits above the first section rather than inside one, so the\n          panel opens with the plugin's own mark and no section rule above it.\n          The QAM is a narrow, dense surface, so this is deliberately small:\n          one fixed width, the artwork's own ratio for the height, and no\n          interaction of any kind.\n\n          The margin is set inline for two reasons. The density stylesheet gives\n          every direct child of the panel a 6px bottom margin, because every\n          other one is a section - this is not, and an inline style is what\n          outranks that rule without deepening the specificity war in\n          `PanelDensity`. The negative top margin then takes back part of the\n          space Decky's own header leaves under the title, so a decorative mark\n          costs the column as little height as possible; the few pixels left\n          underneath keep the artwork off the first section's rule, which it\n          otherwise sits directly on. Width stays an HTML attribute so the\n          artwork is still 112px wide if the density CSS cannot resolve Steam's\n          class names and is not injected at all. */}\n      {mascotVisible && (\n        <div style={{ display: \"flex\", justifyContent: \"center\", padding: 0, margin: \"-8px 0 3px\" }}>\n          <img\n            src={HEXPAW_DATA_URI}\n            alt=\"HexPaw, the CE Decky mascot\"\n            width={112}\n            style={{ width: 112, height: \"auto\", display: \"block\" }}\n          />\n        </div>\n      )}\n      {/* Directly under the mark and above everything the panel is actually\n          for, because it is the one thing here that is not about the game in\n          front of the user and it has to be seen without scrolling a 300 pixel\n          column. It is drawn only when there is a version to offer, so the\n          panel is otherwise exactly what it was: this whole block is absent\n          rather than disabled, which is what keeps it out of the controller's\n          path as well as off the screen.\n\n          Deliberately not asking for the initial focus. Two controls asking is\n          not a preference Steam can settle, and what a panel opens on is\n          already decided between Search and Advanced. */}\n      {/* A section of its own, with Steam's own section row inside it, because\n          that is what the quick access menu walks when the controller moves:\n          the same control in a bare box between the mascot and the first\n          section was drawn hard against the left edge and could not be reached\n          at all. It is the full-width press every other action on this panel\n          is, and it is named like every other row here, because what is on\n          screen is read by test id by the component tests and by the device's\n          own panel reader alike. The box around it carries the colour and\n          nothing else: `CONTENTS_ONLY` keeps it out of the layout, so what\n          Steam lays out and walks is its own row holding its own button,\n          exactly as for every other press on this panel. */}\n      {(updateVersion || updateRunning) && (\n        <PanelSection>\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <div data-testid=\"panel-update\" className={UPDATE_ACTION_CLASS} style={CONTENTS_ONLY}>\n              <ButtonItem\n                layout=\"below\"\n                disabled={busy}\n                onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.update\", onUpdate, { version: updateVersion })}\n              >\n                {updateRunning ? \"Updating CE Decky…\" : `Update to v${updateVersion ?? \"\"}`}\n              </ButtonItem>\n            </div>\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        </PanelSection>\n      )}\n      <PanelSection>\n        <SectionHeading>Setup</SectionHeading>\n        {ceReady ? (\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <PanelRow\n              testId=\"ce-row\"\n              truncate\n              label={ceStatusText}\n              description={ceDetail || \"Ready\"}\n              actions={setupPending ? undefined : (\n                <SmallButton disabled={busy || ceRunning || Boolean(ceIdentityBlockedReason) || !installAvailable} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.reinstall\", onReinstall, { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>{reinstallLabel.startsWith(\"Reinstall\") ? \"Reinstall\" : \"Install\"}</SmallButton>\n              )}\n            />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        ) : (\n          <>\n            <PanelSectionRow><PanelRow testId=\"ce-row\" label=\"Cheat Engine is not installed\" description={ceStatusText} /></PanelSectionRow>\n            {/* Until this succeeds it is the only action the panel is about,\n                so first-run setup keeps a full-width control. */}\n            {!setupPending && !setupStatusError && (\n              <PanelSectionRow><ButtonItem layout=\"below\" disabled={busy || Boolean(ceIdentityBlockedReason) || !installAvailable} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.download_and_install_ce\", () => onInstall(), { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>Download and install CE</ButtonItem></PanelSectionRow>\n            )}\n          </>\n        )}\n        {/* Naming the game that actually holds Cheat Engine is the difference\n            between a dead button and a next step. */}\n        {ceIdentityBlockedReason && (\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <PanelRow testId=\"ce-owned-elsewhere\" truncate label=\"Cheat Engine setup is busy\" description={ceIdentityBlockedReason} />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n        {setupStatusError && (\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <PanelRow\n              testId=\"setup-status-error\"\n              truncate\n              label=\"Setup status unavailable\"\n              description={setupStatusError}\n              actions={<SmallButton disabled={busy} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.retry\", onRetrySetupStatus, { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>Retry</SmallButton>}\n            />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n        {installOperation && (\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <PanelRow\n              testId=\"setup-progress\"\n              truncate\n              label={installOperation.state.replace(/_/g, \" \")}\n              description={`${installOperation.message}${installOperation.error ? ` · ${installOperation.error}` : \"\"}`}\n              actions={installBusy ? <SmallButton disabled={managedCancelling} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.cancel\", onCancelInstall, { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>{managedCancelling ? \"Cancelling…\" : \"Cancel\"}</SmallButton> : undefined}\n            />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n        {installBusy && (\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <div style={{ display: \"flex\", alignItems: \"center\", justifyContent: \"center\", height: 24 }}>\n              <Spinner aria-label=\"CE setup in progress\" style={{ width: 18, height: 18, flexShrink: 0 }} />\n            </div>\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n\n        {/* Automatic detection can land on the wrong library entry, and a user\n            may prepare a table for a game that is not running, so changing the\n            game must never require the Advanced screen. */}\n        <PanelSectionRow>\n          {/* `scroll`: the name of a game and the name of a table are both\n              routinely longer than a 300 pixel column that also carries two\n              presses, and the mark now leading the table's name takes more of\n              that line again. They reveal themselves while the ring is on the\n              row, which is what Manage's rows and a pinned cheat's two lines\n              already do. */}\n          <PanelRow\n            testId=\"game-row\"\n            truncate\n            scroll\n            label={game ? appDetails?.displayName || game.name : \"No game selected\"}\n            description={gameDetail}\n            actions={<SmallButton disabled={workflowBlocked || gameChangeBlocked} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.choose_game\", onChooseGame, { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>{game ? \"Change\" : \"Choose\"}</SmallButton>}\n          />\n        </PanelSectionRow>\n\n        {/* Before the name, not beside the buttons. This row already carries a\n            filename and two presses in a 300 pixel column, and a third thing in\n            the trailing group laid Manage off the edge of the panel - the same\n            arithmetic that kept this row to two controls in the first place.\n            Leading, the mark costs the name's width, which the name can give,\n            and Search and Manage stay where they are on every other row. */}\n        <PanelSectionRow>\n          <PanelRow\n            testId=\"table-row\"\n            truncate\n            scroll\n            label={table ? table.filename : selectedTableMissing ? \"Selected table is missing\" : \"No table selected\"}\n            description={table\n              ? `${tableSource} · ${table.sha256.slice(0, 8)}${tableMarkedNotWorking ? \" · marked as not working\" : \"\"}`\n              : selectedTableMissing ?? \"Search online, or open one this device already has\"}\n            leadingMark={table ? <CompatibilityMark evidence={tableEvidence} blocked={tableBlocked} /> : undefined}\n            actions={(\n              <>\n                <div ref={searchButtonRef} style={CONTENTS_ONLY}>\n                  <SmallButton preferredFocus={openOnSearch} disabled={searchDisabled} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.search\", onSearchTable, { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>Search</SmallButton>\n                </div>\n                {/* Two, because three do not fit. A quick access panel is 300\n                    pixels wide and this row already carries a filename: Search,\n                    Local file and a third control were laid out past the edge on\n                    the device, which is not a row a controller can walk.\n\n                    So everything that is not an online search is behind one\n                    press: the tables this game has, the tables the device has,\n                    opening a local file, and removing one. Manage, because that\n                    screen is where a table is chosen and where it is destroyed,\n                    and a press that only opened things would understate the\n                    second of those.\n\n                    Always present, because it is now the only way to a local\n                    file, and a first run has no table to make it appear. */}\n                <SmallButton disabled={workflowBlocked} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.manage\", onOpenImportedTables, { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>Manage</SmallButton>\n              </>\n            )}\n          />\n        </PanelSectionRow>\n      </PanelSection>\n\n      <PanelSection>\n        <SectionHeading>Cheats</SectionHeading>\n        <PanelSectionRow>\n          {/* A launch this panel owns is the one state where the runtime line\n              has nothing to report but the wait. It used to report the wait as\n              a sequence: the session is prepared, then it is running but not\n              attached, then it is not running for this table again - three\n              descriptions of the same not-yet that the poll cycled through\n              while the user was trying to read one of them. None of them was\n              wrong and none of them was any use, because what is happening is\n              that the launch the user started is still running. */}\n          <PanelRow\n            testId=\"runtime-row\"\n            truncate\n            tone=\"header\"\n            status={runtimeRowStatus}\n            label={launchPending ? \"Starting Cheat Engine\" : tableLoadFailed ? runtimeLabel ?? \"Table not loaded\" : !runtimeReady ? \"Not connected\" : activeCheatSnapshotReady ? activeCheatSummary : \"Connected\"}\n            description={launchPending\n              ? \"Loading the table and waiting for Cheat Engine to answer, usually within fifteen seconds on a handheld. Cancel CE launch below stops it.\"\n              : runtimeHint?.text ?? runtimeText}\n            trailing={launchPending ? <Spinner style={{ width: 14, height: 14 }} /> : undefined}\n          />\n        </PanelSectionRow>\n        {/* Pinning promotes a control onto this panel so the cheats a user\n            actually uses are one press away instead of behind the picker. */}\n        {pinnedRows.map((row) => (\n          <PanelSectionRow key={row.recordId}>\n            <CheatRow\n              variant=\"panel\"\n              testId={`pinned-cheat-${row.recordId}`}\n              label={row.label}\n              summary={row.summary}\n              active={row.active}\n              disabled={workflowBlocked || pinnedBusyRecordId !== null}\n              highlighted={pinnedBusyRecordId === row.recordId}\n              onActiveChange={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.toggle_cheat\", (active) => onTogglePinnedCheat(row.recordId, active), (active) => ({ app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256, record_id: row.recordId, active }))}\n            />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        ))}\n        {pinnedCount > 0 && pinnedRows.length === 0 && !(runtimeReady && activeCheatSnapshotReady) && (\n          <PanelSectionRow><PanelRow status testId=\"pinned-status\" label=\"Pinned controls\" truncate description={`${pinnedCount} pinned; connect Cheat Engine to use them here.`} /></PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n        {runtimeReady && activeCheatSnapshotReady && pinnedMissing > 0 && (\n          <PanelSectionRow><PanelRow status testId=\"pinned-status\" label=\"Pinned controls\" truncate description={`${pinnedMissing} pinned not found in the running table.`} /></PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n        {pinnedCount === 0 && activeCheatLabels.slice(0, 4).map((label, index) => (\n          <PanelSectionRow key={`${index}:${label}`}><PanelRow label={label} truncate /></PanelSectionRow>\n        ))}\n        {pinnedCount === 0 && activeCheatLabels.length > 4 && (\n          <PanelSectionRow><PanelRow label={`+${activeCheatLabels.length - 4} more`} truncate /></PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n\n        {/* A table stays selected across restarts, so the second run must be\n            able to start Cheat Engine again without searching for it again. */}\n        {/* Before the press rather than after it. Starting Cheat Engine against\n            a process this game is not running ends in an attach that never\n            happens, which on this panel looks exactly like Cheat Engine\n            failing, so the press is refused while this stands. Advanced is\n            where it is repaired, because that is where the target lives and\n            where what the game did start is listed. This row is the one that\n            says so wherever the refusal under the press is not on screen. */}\n        {table && targetNotRunning && !startBlockedRowShown && (\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <PanelRow\n              status\n              testId=\"panel-target-not-running\"\n              label={`${targetProcess} is not running in this game`}\n              description={`This game is running ${targetNotRunning.join(\", \")}. Cheat Engine attaches to one exact program, so set the target under Advanced before starting it.`}\n            />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n        {table && !runtimeReady && (\n          <>\n            <PanelSectionRow><ButtonItem layout=\"below\" disabled={workflowBlocked || !startRuntimeAvailable} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.load_table_start_ce\", () => onStartRuntime(), { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>Load table & start CE</ButtonItem></PanelSectionRow>\n            {/* A launch that is running is not a launch that cannot start, and\n                the panel said the second: every reason here is a condition the\n                user has to do something about, and \"Cheat Engine is already\n                running for this game\" told somebody who pressed start twenty\n                seconds ago that their own launch was the obstacle. The runtime\n                line above says what is happening while it happens, so there is\n                nothing left for this row to add. */}\n            {!launchPending && !startRuntimeAvailable && startRuntimeBlockedReason && (\n              <PanelSectionRow><PanelRow status label=\"Cannot start yet\" description={startRuntimeBlockedReason} /></PanelSectionRow>\n            )}\n          </>\n        )}\n        <PanelSectionRow><ButtonItem layout=\"below\" disabled={workflowBlocked || !table} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.configure_cheats\", () => onChooseCheats(), { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>Configure cheats</ButtonItem></PanelSectionRow>\n        {error && <PanelSectionRow><PanelRow testId=\"panel-error\" label=\"Attention\" description={error} /></PanelSectionRow>}\n        {dirtyRunNotice && (\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            <PanelRow\n              testId=\"dirty-run\"\n              truncate\n              label=\"Restart the game first\"\n              description={dirtyRunNotice}\n              actions={<SmallButton disabled={busy} onClick={traceUiAction(\"home_panel.clear_dirty_run\", onClearDirtyRun, { app_id: game?.appId, table_sha: table?.sha256 })}>Clear</SmallButton>}\n            />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        )}\n        {/* Switching everything off, diagnostics and the stop control are rare,\n            so they share one row and never take a full-width button from the\n            cheats. It is a live download route that\n * nothing here needs, and printing it only invites fetching it by hand.\n */\nfunction InstallerProvenance({ ce }: { ce: CEStatus }) {\n  if (!ce.valid) return null;\n  if (!ce.managed) {\n    return (\n      <PanelRow\n        truncate\n        testId=\"ce-provenance-source\"\n        label=\"Cheat Engine source\"\n        description=\"Imported by you\"\n        help=\"This Cheat Engine was imported rather than downloaded by CE Decky, so its origin is whatever you pointed the plugin at. It is verified and usable; only the record is absent. Reinstalling from Home records it.\"\n      />\n    );\n  }\n  const rediscovered = provenance.source === \"rediscovered\";\n  const unrecorded = provenance.source === \"cache\";\n  const signed = provenance.signature_common_name || provenance.signature_subject;\n  return (\n    <>\n      <PanelRow\n        truncate\n        testId=\"ce-provenance-source\"\n        label=\"Cheat Engine source\"\n        description={rediscovered\n          ? \"Downloaded by CE Decky using the current cheatengine.org link\"\n          : unrecorded\n            ? \"Downloaded by CE Decky; the link it used was not recorded\"\n            : \"Downloaded by CE Decky from the reviewed link\"}\n        help={rediscovered\n          ? \"The download link this build of CE Decky ships stopped working, so setup read the current one from the download helper cheatengine.org offers and used that instead. The helper is parsed, never run. What it pointed at still had to be the reviewed release before anything was installed.\"\n          : unrecorded\n            ? \"This artifact was already in CE Decky's own verified cache when setup ran, from a download whose route predates this record. Its bytes are the reviewed release either way - that is what the cache is checked against before it is reused.\"\n            : \"Setup used the exact download link this build of CE Decky ships, and the artifact matched the reviewed release byte for byte.\"}\n      />\n      {/* What vouched for it was a row of its own and said nothing the row\n          below does not: the digest being the reviewed one is the whole reason\n          anything was installed, so \"matches the reviewed release\" was the\n          artifact row restated as a verdict. A source that has never been asked for\n * anything says so instead of showing a row of zeroes, because nothing recorded\n * and everything recorded as zero are different facts.\n */\nfunction describeSource(source: ProviderSourceStatus, countsUnreadable: boolean): string {\n  const counters = source.counters;\n  // Two different reasons for having no counters, and only one of them says\n  // anything about this source: nothing has asked it yet, or the whole record\n  // of what every source has done could not be read.\n  if (!counters) return countsUnreadable ? \"Counts unavailable\" : \"Not searched yet\";\n  const parts = [\n    `${counters.searches} search${counters.searches === 1 ? \"\" : \"es\"}`,\n    `${counters.results} result${counters.results === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"}`,\n  ];\n  // Stated separately, because otherwise a source reached only through another\n  // source's page reads as \"0 searches\" beside a result count nothing on the\n  // row explains.\n  if (counters.linked_reads) parts.push(`${counters.linked_reads} through another source`);\n  if (counters.downloads_succeeded || counters.downloads_failed) {\n    parts.push(`${counters.downloads_succeeded} downloaded${counters.downloads_failed ? `, ${counters.downloads_failed} failed` : \"\"}`);\n  }\n  if (counters.errors) parts.push(`${counters.errors} error${counters.errors === 1 ? \"\" : \"s\"}`);\n  if (counters.parse_failed) parts.push(`${counters.parse_failed} unreadable page(s)`);\n  if (counters.downloads_throttled) parts.push(`${counters.downloads_throttled} rate limit(s) waited out`);\n  // Only while something will actually ask it. A source that is off is not\n  // serving out a wait; the deadline is just what it last said.\n  if (source.enabled && source.cooldown_seconds > 0) parts.push(`waiting ${source.cooldown_seconds}s`);\n  return parts.join(\" · \");\n}\n\n/**\n * The state word for a source, in the user's terms rather than the store's.\n *\n * Absent when this source has never been asked for anything: the description\n * beside it already says so, and repeating it here put the same sentence on the\n * row twice.\n */\nfunction sourceStateLabel(source: ProviderSourceStatus): string | undefined {\n  if (!source.enabled) return \"Off\";\n  if (source.cooldown_seconds > 0) return \"Waiting\";\n  // The last attempt of any kind, search or download: a failed download writes\n  // this state too, so a later successful one now clears it rather than leaving\n  // a source reporting a finished download, no error, and a failed last\n  // attempt at the same time.\n  if (source.state === \"error\") return \"Last attempt failed\";\n  if (source.state === \"ready\") return \"Working\";\n  return undefined;\n}\n\n// The frontend can outlive a reload of an older backend, so a readiness result\n// that predates the directory inventory reports no directories rather than\n// taking the whole screen down with it.\nfunction managedDirectories(removal: RemovalReadiness): RemovalReadiness[\"directories\"] {\n  return removal.directories ?? And it deliberately excludes a script the user switched\n      // on themselves, so doing that by hand brought the whole table's defaults\n      // with it and nothing held them off. A script that was already running\n      // is not here either: its defaults were dealt with when it started, and\n      // writing them again would undo a flag switched on since.\n      //\n      // A script, never a value with flags filed under it: that starts nothing,\n      // and holding its flags off wrote cheats the user had on under a script\n      // that was already running.\n      const startedHere = safeControls.filter((control) => control.id !== null\n        && control.kind === \"script\"\n        && enclosingIds.has(control.id)\n        && activeById.get(control.id) === true\n        && activeBefore.get(control.id) !== true);\n      const heldOff = switchesToHoldOff(startedHere, safeControls, touchedIds);\n      // What the same rule refuses to write: cheats that are on in the game\n      // because this table's own code was not read as surviving them being\n      // switched off. Only this press knows which scripts it started, so this\n      // is where that list comes from.\n      leftOnRef.current = switchesLeftOn(startedHere, safeControls, touchedIds);\n      for (const { control, value } of heldOff) {\n        if (control.id === null) continue;\n        desired.push({\n          record_id: control.id,\n          active: null,\n          value,\n          switch_values: switchValuesFor(control),\n          structure: control.structure,\n          label: controlRowLabel(control),\n          held_off: true,\n        });\n      }\n\n      // Any mutation/revalidation failure after this point makes the previous\n      // Home snapshot stale. Successful final query below republishes a fresh one.\n      //\n      // Both are claims about a write, so neither is made where there is\n      // nothing to write: a press that only stored a value for a script that is\n      // still off touches the game not at all, and saying it did is what puts\n      // \"the game may have been changed\" in front of somebody it was not.\n      if (desired.length > 0) {\n        onSnapshotInvalidated?.();\n        mutatedRuntime = true;\n      }\n      const confirmed = await applyRuntimeSelection(appId, desired);\n      if (confirmed.compatibilityMayHaveChanged) {\n        await onCompatibilityConfirmed?.().catch((cause) => logUiFailure(\"cheats.compatibility_refresh_failed\", cause, { appId }));\n      }\n      // A record the user deliberately switched off may no longer exist, because\n      // its enclosing script created it. Re-query what is still addressable\n      // rather than turning that expected outcome into a failed Apply.\n      const finalState = await queryRuntimeControlsPartial(\n        appId,\n        safeControls.flatMap((control) => control.id === null ? [] : [control.id]),\n        confirmed.envelope,\n      );\n      setUnavailableRecords(new Set(\n        finalState.unavailable.flatMap((result) => result.record_id === null ? [] : [result.record_id]),\n      ));\n      // What the script's own defaults cost, read back rather than assumed: a\n      // flag this did not manage to put down is a cheat running that nobody\n      // asked for, and it is the one thing a later report needs to see.\n      if (heldOff.length > 0) {\n        const finalById = new Map(finalState.results.flatMap(\n          (result) => result.record_id === null ? [] : [[result.record_id, result] as const],\n        ));\n        // Over the scripts that actually held something off, not over the ones\n        // this press manages: a script the reader switched on themselves holds\n        // its defaults off like any other and belongs in the record too.\n        for (const scriptId of new Set(heldOff.map((item) => item.script))) {\n          const mine = heldOff.filter((item) => item.script === scriptId);\n          if (mine.length === 0) continue;\n          logUi(\"runtime.flags_held_off\", {\n            session: confirmed.envelope?.prepared?.session_id ?? null,\n            script_record_id: scriptId,\n            written: mine.length,\n            failed: mine.filter((item) => item.control.id !== null && finalById.get(item.control.id)?.value !== item.value).length,\n          });\n        }\n      }\n      // Cheat Engine answers `??` for an address it cannot read yet, including\n      // every value deliberately deferred above. Keep the\n      // typed value on screen until Cheat Engine reports a real one.\n      const confirmedState: Record<number, StagedState> = {};\n      for (const result of finalState.results) {\n        if (result.record_id === null) continue;\n        const typed = touchedValues.has(result.record_id) ? staged[result.record_id]?.value ?? null : null;\n        confirmedState[result.record_id] = {\n          active: result.active,\n          value: displayableControlValue(result.value) === null ? typed ?? resolvedValue(result.record_id, null) : result.value,\n        };\n      }\n      withWaitingRecords(confirmedState, finalState.results, finalState.unavailable);\n      noteUnreadValues(finalState.results);\n      setStaged(confirmedState);\n      // Cheat Engine has been mutated and verified, but the remembered state\n      // and auto-load are written by the parent. Anything left behind is acknowledged first.\n    if (unsavedCount > 0 || partialCommit) {\n      setConfirmingClose(true);\n      return;\n    }\n    onCancel();\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <ModalRoot onCancel={traceUiAction(\"cheat_selection_modal.request_close\", requestClose)}>\n      <Focusable ref={setWindowNode} style={{ minWidth: 420, maxWidth: 620 }}>\n        <DensePanel>\n        <PanelSection>\n          <SectionHeading>Configure cheats</SectionHeading>\n          <PanelSectionRow>\n            {/* Steam's `verticalAlignment=\"center\"` centres a field's children\n                against its label row, not against the label plus description, so\n                a control beside a two-line summary always sits level with the\n                first line. setFailure(describeError(cause)); })\n      .finally(() => {\n        selectingRef.current = false;\n        setSelecting(false);\n      });\n  };\n  /**\n   * Make the copy of a signed table that this Cheat Engine will open.\n   *\n   * The same latch and the same failure surface as `select`, because it ends\n   * the same way: the parent closes this window and opens Review on the copy,\n   * where the consent for those bytes is given.\n   */\n  const prepareCopy = (sha256: string) => {\n    if (selectingRef.current || !onPrepareCopy) return;\n    setArmed(null);\n    setFailure(null);\n    selectingRef.current = true;\n    setSelecting(true);\n    const operation = startUiOperation(\"manage.prepare_copy\", { table_sha: sha256 });\n    void (async () => onPrepareCopy(sha256))()\n      .then(() => operation.completed())\n      .catch((cause) => { operation.failed(cause); setFailure(describeError(cause)); })\n      .finally(() => {\n        selectingRef.current = false;\n        setSelecting(false);\n      });\n  };\n  /**\n   * Which row's delete has been pressed once, if any.\n   *\n   * The confirmation is the row itself rather than a window over this one. A\n   * modal raised over a modal is a window behind a window, which on the device\n   * is a screen that looks as though the press did nothing, and this project\n   * has already paid for that lesson once. Two presses on the same control,\n   * with the row saying what the second one does, needs no second window and\n   * is a shape a controller can walk. Arming one row disarms any other, and\n   * anything else the reader does with this screen puts it back.\n   */\n  const [armed, setArmed] = useState<string | null>(null);\n  const revoke = (sha256: string) => {\n    if (selectingRef.current || !onRevoke) return;\n    selectingRef.current = true;\n    setSelecting(true);\n    setFailure(null);\n    const operation = startUiOperation(\"manage.revoke\", { table_sha: sha256 });\n    void (async () => {\n      try {\n        await onRevoke(sha256, holderIds[sha256] ?? []);\n        operation.completed();\n        setSelectedBy((current) => ({ ...current, [sha256]: { count: 0, names: [] } }));\n        setActiveSha256((current) => current === sha256 ? null : current);\n      } catch (cause) {\n        operation.failed(cause);\n        setFailure(describeError(cause));\n      } finally {\n        // A multi-holder operation may commit only some withdrawals. Reconcile\n        // that partial result without turning a completed withdrawal into failure.\n        if (onRefreshHolders) {\n          try {\n            const next = await onRefreshHolders();\n            setSelectedBy(next.holders);\n            setHolderIds(next.holderIds ?? {});\n            setActiveSha256(next.activeSha256);\n          } catch (cause) {\n            startUiOperation(\"manage.refresh_holders\", { table_sha: sha256 }).failed(cause);\n          }\n        }\n        selectingRef.current = false;\n        setSelecting(false);\n      }\n    })();\n  };\n  const remove = (sha256: string) => {\n    if (selectingRef.current || !onDelete) return;\n    selectingRef.current = true;\n    setSelecting(true);\n    setFailure(null);\n    const operation = startUiOperation(\"manage.delete\", { table_sha: sha256 });\n    void (async () => onDelete(sha256))()\n      // Only what actually happened. The row goes on the resolution, so a\n      // rejection has to reach here as one: a failure swallowed on the way\n      // would take the row away from a table still on the device.\n      .then(() => {\n        operation.completed();\n        restoreAfterDelete.current = Math.max(0, visible.findIndex((entry) => entry.table.sha256 === sha256));\n        setRemoved((current) => [...current, sha256]);\n      })\n      .catch((cause) => { operation.failed(cause); setFailure(describeError(cause)); })\n      .finally(() => {\n        selectingRef.current = false;\n        setSelecting(false);\n      });\n  };\n  const close = () => {\n    if (!selectingRef.current) onClose();\n  };\n  /**\n   * What a row is called, and what it is doing.\n   *\n   * Which group a row is in is answered by the ground it is drawn on rather\n   * than by a heading, because the two groups are one list so that the screen\n   * has one page budget: a page opening in the middle of the second group\n   * carried no boundary at all, and a run of rows belonging to other games\n   * looked exactly like this game's own. The words remain on the first of them,\n   * for a reader who wants the boundary named.\n   *\n   * In use is in use, whichever game is on it. Saying it only for this game's\n   * own table left a row another game is running looking like any other, with a\n   * missing Delete and nothing on the line to account for it.\n   */\n  const rowLabel = (table: TableStatus, group: \"mine\" | \"device\", index: number): string => {\n    const holders = selectedBy[table.sha256];\n    const holderCount = holders?.count ?? 0;\n    const usedHere = table.sha256 === activeSha256;\n    // One statement, not two. \"in use\" and \"in use by Neon Bazaar\" are the\n    // same sentence on a row that already leads with that game, and the row\n    // carried both. Where this game is the only one on the table the flag is\n    // the whole of it; where others hold it too, naming every one of them is,\n    // and the flag says nothing the naming does not. Needing authorization is\n    // the exception either way: no holder list says that.\n    const soleHolder = usedHere && holderCount <= 1;\n    return [\n      owners?.[table.sha256] ? `${owners[table.sha256]} \\u00b7 ${table.filename}` : table.filename,\n      usedHere && !activeAuthorized ? \"needs authorizing\" : soleHolder ? \"in use\" : null,\n      soleHolder ? null : tableHolderLabel(holders),\n      canSelect && group === \"device\" && (index === 0 || visible[index - 1].group === \"mine\")\n        ? \"elsewhere on this device\"\n        : null,\n    ].filter(Boolean).join(\" · \");\n  };\n  /**\n   * What this row is doing, in a few words, before anything that describes it.\n   *\n   * Every state on this screen answers the same two questions in the same\n   * order: what is up with this row, and which release is it. They used to be\n   * answered the other way round and at length - a row that could not be used\n   * opened with a sentence naming the screen the mark is cleared on, and a row\n   * with a confirmation armed replaced its whole description with a paragraph,\n   * so the release the reader is choosing between was off the end of the line\n   * in exactly the two states where a mistake is expensive.\n   *\n   * Each of these is a state, not a sentence: what follows from it is on the\n   * controls, which say Confirm where a press is armed and offer nothing where\n   * a press is refused, and what it is about is on the line behind it.\n   */\n  const rowStatus = (table: TableStatus): string | null => {\n    const held = (selectedBy[table.sha256]?.count ?? 0) > 0 || table.sha256 === activeSha256;\n    if (armed === table.sha256) {\n      // The consequence in the fewest words that still distinguish the two\n      // presses, because they differ in exactly one way that matters: one keeps\n      // the bytes and the other does not. The bytes here may be the only copy\n      // left - the source may be gone, the row it came from may have changed,\n      // the original file may have been moved - so the delete says what is lost\n      // rather than promising a re-import this screen cannot keep.\n      return held\n        ? `Confirm: revoke and detach \\u00b7 ${tableHolderLabel(selectedBy[table.sha256]) ?? \"held by the current game\"} \\u00b7 local file kept`\n        : \"Confirm: delete from this device \\u00b7 comes back only from a file or a new download\";\n    }\n    // Every state that applies, not the first of them. Returning on the first\n    // match dropped the line that accounts for a missing Delete from exactly\n    // the rows that have one missing for two reasons at once: a table marked as\n    // not working which another game is also holding said only that it was\n    // marked, and the button was gone with nothing on the line explaining it.\n    return [\n      // The reason the one press on this row is off, said before the record it\n      // is off for: a mark this screen shows and Search refuses the same bytes\n      // for is not a mark this screen may quietly step around.\n      // The state and nothing else. Where a mark is cleared and how a damaged\n      // entry is repaired are the same two sentences on every row that has\n      // them, so they say nothing about the row they are on: what belongs here\n      // is what is true of this table, and the release and date behind it are\n      // what the reader came to compare. The routes out are in the README.\n      isCompatibilityFailure(blockedReasons[table.sha256]) ? \"Marked as not working\" : null,\n      !table.available ? \"File missing or damaged\" : null,\n      // Which game has it is on the label, where in use is said for this game's\n      // own table too, so this only has to account for the absent Delete.\n      held ? \"In use, cannot be deleted\" : null,\n    ].filter(Boolean).join(\" \\u00b7 \") || null;\n  };\n  const rowDescription = (table: TableStatus): string => [\n    rowStatus(table),\n    ...describeParts(table),\n    // The mark itself is the glyph on the label, in the same state language\n    // Search uses. What is said here is the head of the recorded sentence behind\n    // it, which is the part a user can act on - and only for a record about\n    // whether the table works. An archive or source failure has no source\n    // context on this screen and belongs to the row it came from and to the\n    // full list under Advanced.\n    isCompatibilityFailure(blockedReasons[table.sha256])\n      ? shortBlockedReason(blockedReasons[table.sha256]?.reason)\n      : null,\n  ].filter(Boolean).join(\" \\u00b7 \");\n  /**\n   * The presses one row carries.\n   *\n   * `Use` is withheld from a table another game owns. A cheat table is written\n   * against one game's code, so applying one game's to another cannot work, and\n   * the press was not merely useless: it associates the table with this game\n   * before the review screen opens, and cancelling that review does not take\n   * the association back. One press on such a row put Half-Life 2's table\n   * permanently into Neon Bazaar's library, where it then read as one of\n   * that game's own tables.\n   *\n   * Owned by another game, not merely listed in the second group. A table this\n   * device holds that no profile claims is the one route back after a recovery\n   * that discards the profile store: the bytes are still here, the association\n   * is gone, and Search needs a provider row while Local file needs the\n   * original file. Offline with neither, this press is the only thing that can\n   * name them, which is what the second group was added for.\n   *\n   * Use keeps the ring wherever it stands: it is what this screen is for, and\n   * it holds the ring through `preferredFocus` rather than by being the first\n   * control, which a signed row's extra press is in front of. Delete is last\n   * and is offered only where deleting is possible at all, so a row for the\n   * table this game is using shows nothing to press.\n   */\n  const rowActions = (table: TableStatus, usable: boolean, group: \"mine\" | \"device\") => (\n    <>\n      {/* Ahead of Use, on the row that carries the amber mark. A signed table\n          is refused with no message at all, so the press that makes the copy\n          which does open belongs where the user is choosing which table to use\n          rather than one screen further in. It consents to nothing: Review\n          opens on the copy and the consent is given there.\n\n          In front rather than among them, because a row lays its controls out\n          from the right: anywhere else, a third press moved Use and whichever\n          of Revoke or Delete the row carries into a different column from every\n          other row, and a list whose buttons do not line up down the screen is\n          what `rowActionStyle` exists to prevent. Measured on a Steam Deck the\n          three of them sit inside the column Steam allows, with about nine\n          pixels to spare, which is why the chip that says why this press is\n          here is drawn in front of the row's name instead of in that column. */}\n      {onPrepareCopy && canSelect && tableIsSigned(table) && table.available\n        && (group === \"mine\" || !owners?.[table.sha256]) && (\n        <div className={PREPARE_ACTION_CLASS} style={CONTENTS_ONLY}>\n          <DialogButton style={rowActionStyle} disabled={selecting}\n            onClick={traceUiAction(\"imported_tables_modal.prepare_copy\", () => prepareCopy(table.sha256), { table_sha: table.sha256 })}\n          >Prepare</DialogButton>\n        </div>\n      )}\n      {canSelect && (group === \"mine\" || !owners?.[table.sha256]) && <DialogButton\n        style={rowActionStyle}\n        preferredFocus={usable}\n        disabled={selecting || !usable}\n        onClick={traceUiAction(\"imported_tables_modal.use\", () => select(table.sha256), { table_sha: table.sha256 })}\n      >Use</DialogButton>}\n      {onRevoke && ((selectedBy[table.sha256]?.count ?? 0) > 0 || table.sha256 === activeSha256) && (\n        <DialogButton style={rowActionStyle} disabled={selecting}\n          onClick={traceUiAction(\"imported_tables_modal.revoke_or_confirm\", () => {\n            if (armed === table.sha256) {\n              setArmed(null);\n              revoke(table.sha256);\n            } else {\n              setFailure(null);\n              setArmed(table.sha256);\n            }\n          }, { table_sha: table.sha256, confirm: armed === table.sha256 })}\n        >{armed === table.sha256 ? \"Confirm\" : \"Revoke\"}</DialogButton>\n      )}\n      {/* Not offered where the answer is already known. Every table a game has\n          selected is refused by the backend, so a press here could only ever\n          spend itself on that refusal, and the row says which game holds it\n          instead of leaving the reader to work out why nothing happened. The\n          backend check stays: this is a snapshot and the answer can change\n          under it. */}\n      {onDelete && !((selectedBy[table.sha256]?.count ?? 0) > 0) && table.sha256 !== activeSha256 && (\n        <DialogButton\n          style={rowActionStyle}\n          disabled={selecting}\n          onClick={traceUiAction(\"imported_tables_modal.delete_or_confirm\", () => {\n            if (armed === table.sha256) {\n              setArmed(null);\n              remove(table.sha256);\n              return;\n            }\n            setFailure(null);\n            setArmed(table.sha256);\n          }, { table_sha: table.sha256, confirm: armed === table.sha256 })}\n        >{armed === table.sha256 ? \"Confirm\" : \"Delete\"}</DialogButton>\n      )}\n    </>\n  );\n  const [filter, setFilter] = useState(\"\");\n  const [page, setPage] = useState(0);\n  /**\n   * Tables this window has removed, which the arrays it was given still hold.\n   *\n   * This screen is opened once with the lists as they were, and the panel that\n   * owns those lists cannot replace the props of a window already on screen. So\n   * a deletion that succeeded left its own row sitting there, offering presses\n   * against bytes that are gone. The window reconciles what it did itself, and\n   * only what actually succeeded: `onDelete` rejects on failure, and a row is\n   * taken away on the resolution rather than on the press.\n   */\n  const [removed, setRemoved] = useState<readonly string[]>([]);\n  /** What went wrong with the last press, said on this screen rather than over it. */\n  const [failure, setFailure] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  /**\n   * Everything this screen can act on, in the order a reader needs it.\n   *\n   * One sequence rather than two lists, because two lists paged separately put\n   * twice the rows on a screen that fits one page of them. The order carries\n   * what the two headings used to: the table this game is on comes first,\n   * because the panel sends the reader here to authorize exactly that one and\n   * sorting it alphabetically could put it pages away; then the rest of this\n   * game's own; then what the device holds for other games.\n   */\n  const entries = useMemo(() => {\n    const needle = filter.trim().toLowerCase();\n    const gone = new Set(removed);\n    const matches = (table: TableStatus) => !gone.has(table.sha256) && (!needle\n      || table.filename.toLowerCase().includes(needle)\n      || table.sha256.startsWith(needle));\n    // Deterministic, so a page does not reshuffle under a thumb: by filename,\n    // then by digest for two tables that share one.\n    const byName = (left: TableStatus, right: TableStatus) =>\n      left.filename.localeCompare(right.filename) || left.sha256.localeCompare(right.sha256);\n    const mine = tables.filter(matches).sort(byName);\n    const active = mine.filter((table) => table.sha256 === activeSha256);\n    const rest = mine.filter((table) => table.sha256 !== activeSha256);\n    const device = otherTables.filter(matches).sort(byName);\n    return [\n      ...active.map((table) => ({ table, group: \"mine\" as const })),\n      ...rest.map((table) => ({ table, group: \"mine\" as const })),\n      ...device.map((table) => ({ table, group: \"device\" as const })),\n    ];\n  }, [tables, otherTables, activeSha256, filter, removed]);\n  const [listNode, setListNode] = useState<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);\n  const [footerNode, setFooterNode] = useState<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);\n  // What this screen actually fits, read from the screen. It was the one paged\n  // list here that measured nothing and took six as an answer, and six ran off\n  // the bottom of a Steam Deck's 534 pixel page. Nothing on this screen is\n  // transient, so the first credible measurement is the settled one.\n  const [chrome, setChrome] = useState<LatchedChrome | null>(null);\n  useLayoutEffect(() => {\n    setChrome((held) => latchChrome(held, listNode, footerNode, MODAL_BOTTOM_PADDING));\n  }, [listNode, footerNode]);\n  const tableRowHeight = useRowHeight(listNode, MANAGE_ROW_HEIGHT);\n  const asked = useMemo(() => (chrome === null ? This is the screen that made the rule worth having: it measured\n  // what was above its list before the filter had been drawn, and the page it\n  // sized from that ran 27 pixels behind the bar.\n  const fitted = useFittedRows(footerNode, tableRowHeight, chrome !== null, entries.length > asked, failure ? 1 : 0);\n  // Never past the page this screen was built with, for the same reason\n  // `rowsThatFit` caps there: room found after the fact is not a reason to\n  // change a screen that had no problem.\n  const pageSize = Math.min(MANAGE_PAGE_SIZE, Math.max(1, asked + fitted));\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!listNode) return;\n    logUi(\"manage.page_sized\", {\n      viewport: viewportHeight(listNode), chrome: chrome?.value ?? null, rows: pageSize, fitted,\n    });\n  }, [pageSize, listNode, chrome, fitted]);\n  const pages = pageCount(entries.length, pageSize);\n  const safePage = clampPage(page, entries.length, pageSize);\n  const visible = pageItems(entries, safePage, pageSize);\n  // A page of rows is held at the height a page of rows takes, measured off the\n  // rows themselves. Every row on this list is one line of name over one line\n  // of state, so one of them times a page is what a page costs, and the window\n  // stays where it is on the last page and on a device whose whole library is\n  // three tables and never fills one.\n  const pageHeight = usePageHeight(listNode, visible.length, pageSize);\n  // What this screen still has, which is what it was given minus what it has\n  // removed. Paging the row away and coming back to it\n   * hours later must not find it still armed and one press from destroying a\n   * file, so every navigation here disarms it.\n   */\n  const moveTo = (next: () => void) => {\n    setArmed(null);\n    setFailure(null);\n    next();\n  };\n  return (\n    <ModalRoot onCancel={traceUiAction(\"imported_tables_modal.close\", close)} onEscKeypress={traceUiAction(\"imported_tables_modal.close_2\", close)}>\n      <DensePanel tightRows>\n        {/* First, and one row tall. It is the only way to a local file and the\n            only thing here that works on a device holding nothing, and a list\n            of tables is exactly what a reader never scrolls to the end of: put\n            below several pages of them it may as well not exist.\n\n            Drawn whether or not a game is chosen, and pressable either way.\n            The file joins this device's library with no game at all, which is\n            what the backend has always allowed; what waits for a game is the\n            association and the authorization, and Use on the row this import\n            produces is where those happen. It is reviewed and authorized like any other.\"\n              actions={(\n                <SmallButton\n                  disabled={selecting || !onOpenLocalFile}\n                  onClick={traceUiAction(\"imported_tables_modal.local_file\", () => {\n                    // The prop stays optional: a screen opened without this\n                    // route may not press it.\n                    if (!onOpenLocalFile) return;\n                    // This window first: Decky's picker is a modal of its own,\n                    // and one raised over another is a window behind a window.\n                    onClose();\n                    onOpenLocalFile();\n                  })}\n                >Local file</SmallButton>\n              )}\n            />\n          </PanelSectionRow>\n        </PanelSection>\n        <PanelSection>\n          <SectionHeading>Tables</SectionHeading>\n          {/* Said here, on the screen the press was made on. A window raised\n              over this one is a window behind a window on the device, and the\n              row this is about is still in front of the reader. */}\n          {failure && (\n            <PanelSectionRow>\n              <PanelRow testId=\"manage-failure\" status label=\"That did not work\" description={failure} />\n            </PanelSectionRow>\n          )}\n          {remaining.length === 0 && (\n            <PanelSectionRow>\n              <Field\n                label=\"Nothing imported yet\"\n                description=\"Open a file above, or search online.\"\n              />\n            </PanelSectionRow>\n          )}\n          {remaining.length > 0 && entries.length === 0 && (\n            <PanelSectionRow>\n              <Field label=\"Nothing matches that\" description=\"Clear the filter to see every table.\" />\n            </PanelSectionRow>\n          )}\n          {/* The row that heads the list, drawn as one. As an ordinary field it\n              was the same weight as the tables under it, so the first thing on\n              the list looked like the first table on it. `tone=\"header\"` is the\n              shape this panel already uses for a row that names what follows:\n              its own ground, an accent, and a gap under it holding the rows off\n              itself.\n\n              One short line under it. It carried three sentences explaining\n              that choosing a table associates it and opens the review screen,\n              which is what the next press shows the reader anyway, and it wrapped\n              to three lines of a page that is counted in rows. What is left is\n              the part that is not obvious from doing it: this screen needs\n              neither a source nor a network. */}\n          {/* The filter rides on the row that heads the list rather than taking\n              a row of its own. A row each is what Steam's own components do,\n              and on a Steam Deck this one cost 46 of 534 pixels for a control\n              holding at most a few characters - which is one table off the\n              page, on the screen whose whole job is listing them. Its word is\n              inside the box, as the placeholder, where it is gone the moment\n              there is anything to read.\n\n              In the row's action group and not beside its trailing text: that\n              slot is for a word, it is dimmed and set small on purpose, and a\n              row whose only control sat there would not be wrapped in anything\n              the controller can enter.\n\n              Drawn whenever the filter is reachable, not only when the list\n              has rows in it: a filter that matches nothing empties the list,\n              and a filter that disappears with the last row it matched is one\n              nobody can clear.\n\n              Its line is short because the filter beside it takes the width\n              that line is not using, and a sentence that does not fit is a\n              sentence nobody reads; `scroll` reveals whatever still clips while\n              the reader is on the row.\n\n              It is also the only thing heading this list in either state. The current installation keeps working until the replacement is verified, and setup can be cancelled at any time.\"\n          strOKButtonText=\"Reinstall\"\n          strCancelButtonText=\"Cancel\"\n          onOK={traceUiAction(\"panel.reinstall.confirm\", () => { confirm.Close(); startManagedSetup(capability, true); })}\n          onCancel={traceUiAction(\"panel.reinstall.cancel\", () => confirm.Close())}\n        />,\n      );\n      return;\n    }\n    startManagedSetup(capability, force);\n  };\n\n  /** Explain a setup that could not obtain Cheat Engine by any route.\n   *\n   * Both download routes failing is the one setup outcome the user cannot act\n   * on from the panel itself, and a one-line error under the button does not\n   * carry the way out. Install Cheat Engine on a Windows machine\n              from cheatengine.org, then bring its installation folder to this device -\n              copy the folder across, or pack it into a .zip. Import it from\n              Advanced, under Registered Cheat Engine. Everything after that works\n              exactly as a downloaded Cheat Engine does.\n            </p>\n          </div>\n        )}\n        strOKButtonText=\"Close\"\n        onOK={traceUiAction(\"panel.setup_failure.close\", () => dialog.Close())}\n        onCancel={traceUiAction(\"panel.setup_failure.cancel\", () => dialog.Close())}\n      />,\n    );\n  };\n\n  const unavailable.\");\n      return;\n    }\n    // The dialog belongs to setup failing, not to the panel refusing a press.\n    // Catching inside the action makes that structural: a press refused because\n    // another operation is running never reaches this body at all.\n    void runAction(async () => {\n      try {\n        await runManagedSetup(force);\n      } catch (cause) {\n        showManagedSetupFailure(describeError(cause));\n        throw cause;\n      }\n    }, { failureShownByCaller: true }).catch(() => undefined);\n  };\n\n  const cancelManagedSetup = async () => {\n    const owner = managedOwnerRef.current;\n    const operation = owner?.operation;\n    if (!owner || !operation || !operationIsActive(operation) || managedCancelRef.current) return;\n    managedCancelRef.current = true;\n    setManagedCancelling(true);\n    const cancellation = startUiOperation(\"managed_setup.cancel\", { operation_id: operation.operation_id });\n    try {\n } catch (cause) {\n      cancellation.failed(cause);\n      logUiFailure(\"managed_setup.cancel_failed\", cause, { operation_id: operation.operation_id });\n      setError(describeError(cause));\n    } finally {\n      managedCancelRef.current = false;\n      setManagedCancelling(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const requestOwnedCEStop = async (appId: number, tableSha256?: string, holdAutoload = false): script's `[DISABLE]`, which is what puts the game's bytes back. The user\n    // consented to this exact table executing, so it is inside the boundary,\n    // and they are told rather than surprised.\n    //\n    // Worded as what the stop does rather than as what is happening now. The\n    // panel cannot know yet whether there is anything on to switch off, and a\n    // stop with a disconnected bridge would otherwise announce work that never\n    // took place.\n    // A stop the user asked for holds Auto-load for this run of the game, and\n    // the switch still reads on: without this sentence the reader would wonder\n    // why nothing started again, or wait for it to.\n    const armed = holdAutoload\n      && selectedGameRef.current?.appId === appId\n      && currentProfile(statusRef.current, selectedGameRef.current)?.autoload_enabled === true;\n    toaster.toast({\n      title: \"CE Decky\",\n      body: \"Stopping Cheat Engine. []).join(\",\") || null,\n    });\n    // The one outcome worth interrupting somebody for: a cheat that is still on\n    // in a game that has just lost the Cheat Engine which could have switched\n    // it off. Nothing later can undo it - the restore reads symbols belonging\n    // to a process that is gone - so restarting the game is the whole answer.\n    const left = quiesce?.records_unsettled ?? Restart the game to clear what they changed.`,\n      });\n    } else if (quiesce?.cleanup_confirmed === false) {\n      // Not knowing is the same news as a named cheat, and for the same reason:\n      // the stop went ahead without it, so whatever was still on is still on,\n      // and the Cheat Engine that could have switched it off is gone. Every\n      // way of not knowing counts: an answer that never came, an address list\n      // that could not be read, a bridge that went quiet while the game is\n      // still running. Saying nothing for those reported them as a clean stop.\n      toaster.toast({\n        title: \"CE Decky\",\n        body: \"Cheat Engine stopped before CE Decky could confirm your cheats were switched off. If anything is still changed in the game, restarting it clears that.\",\n      });\n    }\n    if (result.recovered && !result.stopped) {\n      throw new Error(\"CE Decky could not prove that the owned Cheat Engine process stopped; the session was left unchanged.\");\n    }\n    dropLiveSnapshot();\n    return { stopped: result.stopped, cleanupConfirmed: quiesce?.cleanup_confirmed ?? null, unsettled: left };\n  };\n\n  const stopOwnedCE = async (appId: number, tableSha256?: string, holdAutoload = false): Promise<OwnedStopVerdict> => {\n    const verdict = await requestOwnedCEStop(appId, tableSha256, holdAutoload);\n    await refreshCELaunch(appId).catch(() => undefined);\n    await refreshRuntime(appId).catch(() => undefined);\n    return verdict;\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Name the cheats a successful startup left on that nobody chose.\n   *\n   * Every path that says a startup succeeded owes this, because what it says is\n   * about the cheats the user chose and these are running beside them: a script\n   * startup started brought its author's defaults, and the ones whose code was\n   * not read as surviving being written off stay on. The backend answers from\n   * the same plan the session was prepared from; an answer about another table\n   * than the one this path loaded says nothing about it.\n   */\n  const announceStartupLeftOn = async (appId: number, tableSha: string, controls: readonly TableControl[]) => {\n    try {\n      const answer = await startupLeftOn(appId);\n      if (answer.table_sha256 !== tableSha || answer.record_ids.length === 0) return;\n      const ids = new Set(answer.record_ids);\n      const sentence = leftOnSentence(controls.filter((control) => control.id !== null && ids.has(control.id)));\n      if (sentence) toaster.toast({ title: \"CE Decky\", body: sentence });\n    } catch (cause) {\n      logUiFailure(\"startup.left_on_unread\", cause, { app_id: appId });\n    }\n  };\n\n  const ensureAttachedRuntime = async (\n    game: GameSummary, process: string, report: StepReporter = () => undefined, automatic = false,\n  ): Promise<RuntimeEnvelope> => {\n    report(\"Starting Cheat Engine\");\n    const capability = await refreshCELaunch(game.appId);\n    if (!capability.ce_ready) throw new Error(capability.reason || \"Cheat Engine is not ready.\");\n    if (!capability.game?.running) throw new Error(capability.game?.reason || \"The selected game is not running.\");\n    // The backend launch transaction prepares the session itself, so preparing\n    // one here only wrote a second exact-SHA table snapshot that Cheat Engine\n    // never opened; both were retained.\n    logUi(\"panel.launch_requested\", {\n      app_id: game.appId, process,\n      proton: capability.observed_proton_tool?.tool_id ?? null,\n      game_running: capability.game?.running ?? false,\n      windows_executables: (capability.game?.windows_executables ?? []).join(\",\"),\n      automatic,\n    });\n    // Said to the backend rather than only checked here: the hold a Stop takes\n    // on Auto-load is the backend's, and a panel that read no hold a moment\n    // ago is not the authority on whether one is there now.\n    const started = await launchCEForGame(game.appId, capability.observed_proton_tool?.tool_id ?? null, automatic);\n    // Adopt the owned operation before waiting on it, so Home can show and stop\n    // a launch that is still waiting for the bridge.\n    setCELaunchOperation(started);\n    setLaunchInProgress({ appId: game.appId, operationId: started.operation_id });\n    // The launch is adopted, so from here there is an exact owned operation to\n    // stop, and it stays stoppable through attach: what is running is the same\n    // Cheat Engine either way.\n    report(\"Waiting for Cheat Engine to load the table and answer\", true);\n    let operation: CELaunchStatus;\n    try {\n      operation = await awaitLaunchOutcome(started);\n    } finally {\n      setLaunchInProgress(null);\n    }\n    if (operation.state !== \"connected\") {\n      logUiWarning(\"panel.launch_not_connected\", {\n        app_id: game.appId, state: operation.state,\n        message: operation.message, error: operation.error,\n      });\n      throw new Error(operation.error || operation.message || \"Cheat Engine did not connect to the game session.\");\n    }\n    logUi(\"panel.launch_connected\", { app_id: game.appId, session: operation.session_id.slice(0, 12) });\n    setCELaunchOperation(operation);\n    void refreshCELaunch(game.appId).catch(() => undefined);\n    let observed = await refreshRuntime(game.appId);\n    if (!observed.connected || observed.prepared?.session_id !== operation.session_id || observed.status?.session_id !== operation.session_id) {\n      throw new Error(\"Cheat Engine started, but the exact fresh bridge session was not confirmed.\");\n    }\n    if (!observed.status?.attached) {\n      const exact = (observed.status?.processes ?? []).filter(([, name]) => name.toLowerCase() === process.toLowerCase());\n      if (exact.length === 1) {\n        report(`Attaching to ${process}`, true);\n        const [pid, name] = exact[0];\n        const attached = await sendRuntimeCommandAndWait(game.appId, { kind: \"retry_attach\", value: name, target_pid: pid });\n        observed = attached.envelope;\n        setRuntime(observed);\n      }\n    }\n    // Attached is not loaded. A Cheat Engine that could not open the table\n    // attaches to the game anyway and reports itself perfectly healthy, with an\n    // address list that answers \"missing\" for every record: nothing to switch\n    // on, nothing to pin, no live value to read. Every caller here is asking\n    // for a runtime it can use, and all three of them used to say \"Table\n    // loaded\" for this one, leaving Home's own row as the only account of it.\n    if (observed.status?.table_load_state === \"failed\") {\n      logUiWarning(\"panel.table_not_loaded\", {\n        app_id: game.appId, route: observed.status?.table_load_route ?? null,\n        error: observed.status?.table_load_error ?? null,\n      });\n      throw new Error(\n        observed.status?.table_load_error\n        || \"Cheat Engine started and attached to the game, but it could not open this table.\",\n      );\n    }\n    return observed;\n  };\n\n  const ensureProfileAssociation = async (sha256: string): Promise<void> => {\n    const game = selectedGameRef.current;\n    if (!game) throw new Error(\"No game is selected.\");\n    let profile = currentProfile(await refreshStatus(), game);\n    if (!profile) {\n      // Exact desired state, so a lost reply is asked about rather than\n      // reported as a failed import of a table the backend has already stored.\n      await commitDesiredState({\n        subject: \"the profile for this game\",\n        write: () => saveProfile(game.appId, appDetails?.displayName || game.name, game.isShortcut, null, null),\n        verify: async () => Boolean(currentProfile(await refreshStatus(), game)),\n      });\n      // Ask the authority again rather than reusing what this screen last saw.\n      // `commitDesiredState` returns the moment its write succeeds and re-reads\n      // only when the reply was lost, so on the ordinary path nothing had\n      // refreshed the status since before this profile existed: the cached one\n      // still held no profile for the game, and a first table that had just\n      // been downloaded, verified and stored ended in \"could not create the\n      // game profile\" for a profile that was on disk.
