Once the wait for the backend had to outlive a whole doomed generation rather than sample one, the same install measured 38.9 s |
```md
| What Game Mode gives the frontend to lay out in | Both machines, 2026-09-07, `scripts/target_ui_layout_probe.py`, read from Steam's own pages. Valve Steam Machine on a 4K display and Steam Deck LCD on its 1280x800 panel, CE Decky 0.9.18, Decky Loader 3.2.8 | Steam picks a device pixel ratio for the display and scales its whole UI, so the frontend never sees physical pixels and the CSS viewport is the whole of what a layout has to fit. The page a modal opens in is **1500 x 844** CSS pixels on the Steam Machine at a ratio of 2.56, and **854 x 534** on the handheld at 1.5; the quick access panel is 855 x 765 against 854 x 454. Both products of ratio and viewport come back to the panel's own resolution, so the ratio is the whole of the difference. The width is within one pixel on the two machines and the height is 310 pixels apart, so a screen that does not fit a handheld is never too wide: it is too tall, and by an amount no screenshot can report, because a capture is in output pixels and the ratio between the two is exactly what is unknown. Re-read on 2026-09-08 with CE Decky 0.9.20 for the context this plugin's own code runs in, which is not any of those pages: `SharedJSContext` reports a viewport of **1 x 1** and a screen of **1 x 1**, while `QuickAccess_uid2` reports 854 x 454 and the Big Picture page 854 x 534 on the same device at the same moment. `MainMenu_uid2` and `notificationtoasts_uid2` also report a 1 x 1 viewport while reporting the real 853 x 533 screen, so a 1 x 1 viewport is not by itself a context with nothing in it |
| How large a real table's value lists get | 2026-09-05, a 1.4 MB table of 323 entries served as `.rar` | Three item pickers of 6508 values each, the largest 268.6 KiB of text. A 4096-value ceiling would have dropped 2412 items from each; a byte ceiling below 268.6 KiB refused the whole table. The ceilings are now 1 MiB and 16384, and exceeding the byte ceiling drops that one list and counts it |

## 2. Observed behaviour, and what it forced

| Observed | Why the obvious approach does not work |
|---|---|
| Decky v3.3.0's frozen Python 3.14.8 omits pathlib.types, disabling the packaged anyio async backend | Steam Machine, SteamOS 3.8.28, 2026-10-18, CE Decky 0.9.29. All five provider searches and the updater logged `Running with asyncio requires installation of 'httpcore[asyncio]'`. A separate process of the exact installed PluginLoader reproduced anyio 4.14.2 failing on `from pathlib.types import PathInfo`; httpcore swallowed that ImportError and retained `anyio=None`. Loading verbatim CPython v3.14.8 `Lib/pathlib/types.py` only in the disposable process restored the async lock and production HTTPS get/download; a fresh process without it failed again. The runtime dependency was already present, so reinstalling it does not supply the missing standard-library module. The production supplement belongs before the first anyio/httpcore import, only on Python 3.14 and only for that exact missing module. The tracked `scripts/decky_compat_probe.py` now reproduces packaged behavior without a live plugin or user-state access; its route is diagnostic, not a Decky API. These observations did not establish a completed user search before installation of the repair |
| Python 3.14 status predicates can turn access denial into apparently missing managed state | Same machine and frozen runtime, disposable directories only, compared with system Python 3.13.5 on 2026-10-18. | Writing a table's own flag off can kill the game minutes later, and only the table's own code says whether it will | Steam Machine, 2026-09-21, table `2ce741d9` against the game it was written for, from that game's own minidump written one minute after the cheat was switched on: `EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x48`, `Rcx=0x48`, `Rsi=0x9190ad50`, and a faulting instruction no module covers - Cheat Engine's own allocation. That table still read 17 of 22 and the 12 tables 51 of 67 after those, so on these tables they cost nothing, and what they close is a proof that could otherwise stand on code the reader never walked. What moved it to 14 and 44 is a load into a register, a push or a pop made after a flag is tested: that is one side of the branch handing the game a register or a stack the other side does not, and the reader does not know which side is off. The three flags that table lost are real instances rather than an artefact of the rule: their hooks load `r10` with `movsx`/`movsxd` or convert into `r8d` with `cvtss2si` behind the flag and return to the game with it. What a hook loads into a scratch register is still not a finding: it happens whichever way the flag goes, so it is never the difference between the cheat being on and the game being handed something it cannot use. | Decky's own stop spins the plugin's event loop, so `_unload()` never resumes past its first `await` | Steam Machine, Decky Loader v3.2.8, 2026-09-13. When Decky stops the plugin, every record `_unload()` writes without suspending appears and nothing after its first real `await` does: the loop runs a callback queued with `call_soon` and never fires a `call_later(0.5)` timer, and SIGKILL arrives five seconds later. The control case settles it: one SIGTERM sent by hand, with no other part of Decky's stop, completes the whole unload in 18 ms, drain included, and logs `backend.unload_completed`. What Decky does besides the signal is close its end of the plugin's Unix socket, immediately after `proc.terminate()`, by cancelling its response listener. Both ends of that socket then read at EOF in a loop that cannot suspend: `localsocket.py` `_read_single_line` returns `""` at EOF without awaiting, and both `_listen_for_method_call` in the plugin process and `_response_listener` in the loader call it inside `while` loops that swallow the result, so the loop is monopolised and no task, callback or timer behind it ever runs. The loader half of the same defect was measured directly here at exactly one saturated core after a plugin process died. What this forces: nothing an unload must finish may sit behind an `await`, because when Decky is the one stopping the plugin there is no guarantee anything after the first one runs. Plugin state is kept safe by atomic replacement and recovery on the next load, not by the drain. Still unobserved: the plugin process's own CPU during a Decky-initiated stop, which is what would show its half of the spin directly rather than by the loader's |

| SteamOS with Decky Loader 3.2.8 ran CE Decky's backend as the Steam user while `kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=1`; an explicit-PID `target_decky_env_probe.py` read still reported that one process unreadable | Installation authority cannot depend on a sibling development process reading the backend's environment. It comes through Decky's authenticated inventory plus the exact path the backend received from Decky, with a durable XDG record only as the offline fallback |
| Gamescope runs more than one XWayland server, and Steam and the game do not share one | Cheat Engine joining the game's prefix on Steam's display makes Wine's X11 driver operate on window identities from another server, and the process ends on the Xlib default error handler. The display comes from the game's own environment |
| Steam's gamepad toggle is a fixed 38x22 box whose 22px knob is absolutely positioned | A flex row's default `flex-shrink: 1` narrows the box while the knob keeps its geometry, so the switch paints clipped over whatever is beside it. The box is pinned |
| `PanelSectionRow > :first-child` publishes `--field-negative-horizontal-margin: 16px` | Compact field padding resolves to `padding: 10px 0` plus that negative inline margin, so a row hangs 16px off the left edge and its buttons are clipped by the right one |
| A phpBB listing may render its current page number as a non-link | That page then exposes no independent stride evidence, so page zero stays the only authority that establishes index geometry and a later page may only reuse a proven stride |
| A program started under Proton can run while the window it opens is unreachable in Gamescope | Reported against other projects on some Proton 11 and Experimental combinations, in `SheffeyG/CheatDeck` issue 84 and `ValveSoftware/Proton` issue 9999. It is why readiness here is the resident bridge's heartbeat and never a visible window, and why a mapped Cheat Engine window is treated as a failure to correct rather than a sign of success |
| Steam consults a container's `navEntryPreferPosition` only when the movement that reaches it carries no rectangle | Read in `steamui/library.js`, `FindFocusableDescendant`: a rectangle, or a geometric layout with a direction, takes the closest-node branch and the stated preference is never reached; `PREFERRED_CHILD` is the branch after it. The same `preferredFocus` therefore places the ring on Next in a modal footer, whose parent is one of this plugin's own columns, and does nothing in the QAM, where Decky's `PanelSection` is a plain div and the row's parent is Steam's own panel. Moving the ring out of Steam's transfer with `HTMLElement.focus()` is not the way around it: it was tried on the device, and while the ring did land on the intended control, Steam's tree went on pointing at the control it had itself chosen. A press then activated nothing, and the row above became unreachable, until a left or right press re-synchronised the two. The visible ring and the node Steam will act on are separate pieces of state, and only Steam's own transfer moves both. The branch that does run sorts a row's controls by distance from that rectangle, which is equal for every control on one row, and then by how much of its width each one covers, so a vertical step into a row lands on the widest control and the order of the controls settles only an exact tie. That width is the lever, and it is the only one |
| Gamescope's statistics pipe reports composited frames, which are capped at the panel's refresh rate | A game on a Steam Deck read as exactly 60.00 with zero variance across a 30-second window while the game's own counter showed about 113, and the same pipe reads a real spread as soon as the game falls below 60. A game with frames to spare therefore cannot show what anything costs it, and raising graphics settings does not help while the engine still outruns the panel. The measurement is made by removing the headroom instead: the device is held at a power limit low enough that the game is the constraint, which is also the condition the handheld question is actually about. Seen a second time on 2026-09-07 in the other direction: with no power limit the pipe read a steady 56 while the game's own overlay showed a steady 38, so the composited rate and the application rate differ in both directions and neither substitutes for the other. The pipe also does **not** write once a second, which this row used to say. Read straight off it with `cat`, it wrote a rate-and-focus pair every 5.3 seconds on the Deck and about every 7.5 on the Steam Machine, both steady. A 90-second window therefore holds a dozen readings rather than ninety, and every within-window spread recorded here rests on that many points. The probe measures the interval and reports it beside the rate rather than assuming one |
| SteamOS reports `VARIANT_ID=steamdeck` on a Steam Machine as well as on a Steam Deck | `/etc/os-release` identifies the distribution and never the device, so a helper that has to know which machine it is on reads DMI instead: `sys_vendor` is `Valve` and `product_name` is `Fremont` on the Steam Machine, `Jupiter` on the Steam Deck LCD and `Galileo` on the OLED. Read on the Steam Machine on 2026-09-07 under SteamOS 3.8.16, build 20260716.1; the two Deck names are upstream's and are not confirmed here |
| `/proc/<pid>/io` is denied for this plugin's own backend, to the same user that runs it | The same non-dumpable protection already recorded for `/proc/<pid>/environ`. Byte and syscall counters would have been the most direct reading of polling and are unavailable for the one process the cost question is about; they are readable for Cheat Engine and for the game. The cost probe records the refusal rather than omitting the field, because an absent counter and a counter that did not move look identical otherwise |
| One catalog's page-supplied byte count can differ from a valid artifact by one byte | An advertised size is display metadata; an advertised SHA-256 is the integrity authority |
| Decky keeps five per-load log files per plugin, and one install produces several loads | Read on the Steam Machine on 2026-09-12: every plugin directory under `~/homebrew/logs` held at most five `.log` files, and CE Decky's five had all been written inside one 45-second install cycle. The 90 minutes of backend activity before it, which was the session being diagnosed, no longer existed anywhere. So the plugin log answers a question only while the plugin has not been reinstalled since it was asked, and installing the build that would answer it is what destroys the evidence. Reproducing a fault therefore means installing first and reproducing afterwards, and anything a later failure has to be diagnosed from has to survive a reload on its own |
| Cheat Engine refuses a signed `.CT` by returning `false` from `loadTable`, with nothing on screen and nothing in its own log | Steam Machine, 2026-09-20, Cheat Engine 7.7 `9727076d`. The three tables this device holds for one game, `33a60e6b` and `bc775640` written as table version 52 and `7f995066` as 42, each carry a `<Signature>` element holding a `SignedHash` and a `PublicKey`, and all three failed identically: the bridge's `loadTable(stream, false, true)` returned `false` inside a second, `table_load=failed table_load_route=approved` with `address_list_count=0`, and no form was raised, `dialogs_dismissed=none` and `window_suppressions=0`. The same bytes with the `<Signature>` element removed, imported as `fac00ebb`, loaded on the next launch with all 52 records. Every other table this device holds is unsigned and none shows the failure. The installed binary carries the refusals this belongs to, `This table has been modified. To load this table, remove the signature part with an editor`, `The provided public key is invalid(Not signed by the Cheat Engine guy). Remove the signature section to load this table` and `Could not open the algorithm provider. Load the table as if it's signature is valid?` beside `BCryptVerifySignature`, so which of them ran is not established and the returned `false` is the whole of what was proved. Nothing in this project reads a table's signature, so a signed table is offered, authorized and prepared like any other and the panel can only report what the bridge saw |
| This Cheat Engine refuses every signed `.CT` put in front of it, and the question can be asked in four seconds without a game | Steam Machine, 2026-09-20, Cheat Engine 7.7 `9727076d` under GE-Proton11-7, through `scripts/target_ce_launch_probe.py --table`. **16 of 16** tables carrying a `<Signature>` were refused, all with `table_load_error=Cheat Engine refused to open the table`, `table_load_route=approved`, `address_list_count=0`, no form raised and a clean stop; the 16 span 8 distinct `PublicKey` blobs and table versions 29 to 52, so this is not one signer or one format generation. Two unsigned controls loaded in the same harness with 52 and 30 records, which is what makes the result a property of the signature rather than of the probe. The probe costs 4.1 s, measured three times on this machine, because the bridge loads the session table in its bootstrap before the attach and does not depend on a target process, so `prepare_self_test_session` given exact bytes answers for any `.CT` with no game, no profile and no Steam state. What is still not established is why: Cheat Engine's own strings offer a modified-table refusal, a public-key refusal and a `BCryptVerifySignature` provider failure, the last of which is Wine rather than the table, and nothing here separates them. The load runs the table's Lua, so this check is execution and belongs behind consent for it |
| A pattern that matches twice cannot be told from one that matches once without reading the whole program | Steam Machine, 2026-09-21, the anchor table's 28 patterns against its 407 MiB program. Stopping at the first match: **0.69 s**. Counting to two for every pattern with `finditer`: **4.08 s**, six times the cost. That run reported all 27 present patterns as matching once, and it was wrong, because `finditer` skips a match overlapping the one before it: the shipped rule, which looks again from one byte past the first match, finds `aobPlayerStatsOffset` matching twice **16 bytes apart** in that same program - two consecutive getters of the same shape, the second reading a different field offset, and Cheat Engine would take either. Looking once more inside the span the first match was already read from costs **0.03 s** and finds a second place that is actually there, which is why the product reports that and never reports uniqueness. Cheat Engine's own `celua.txt` is the reason it is worth reporting at all: `AOBScanUnique` is documented as returning "any random match", so a pattern the author did not make unique is a hook that lands wherever the scan happened to stop |
| Stopping owned Cheat Engine while an Auto Assembler script is active leaves the game patched, and the next session cannot switch that script on again | Steam Machine, 2026-09-20, one game and the same table SHA `8e3574a1` across two sessions. Session `112d68ad` enabled the table's one Auto Assembler record and the bridge confirmed it, `ok=1 active=1`, with every symbol the script registers reading a real value. The panel's reconnect then ran `stop_ce_for_game` and launched `30c3e031`, and in that session the same record answered `activation timed out`, which is `AsyncProcessing` still true after `MAX_ACTIVATION_WAIT_TICKS` at `POLL_MS`, ten seconds, and it was still off and still `??` a minute later. The game process carries the reason: read through `/proc/<pid>/mem` over the module's own text at `0x140001000`, four of the script's scan targets, `aobAmmoTaker`, `aobItemTaker`, `aobJumpSpeedCalc` and `aobSightConeCalc`, are absent from memory while present in the executable on disk, the two that are read sites rather than injection sites, `aobWeaponOwnerOffset` and `aobPlayerStatsOffset`, are intact, and an 8 KB `rwxp` mapping sits inside the text at `0x14365c000`. So the first session's `jmp` patches and its allocation outlive it: the stop kills the owned process group and `[DISABLE]` never runs, and the restore that block performs reads symbols that belonged to the dead Cheat Engine, so no later session can undo it either. Nothing short of restarting the game gives a scan its original bytes back. The stop path does not deactivate what is active first, which is what turns an ordinary table switch or reconnect into this |

## 3. Boundaries of these observations

| Behaviour | Seen on | Not seen on |
|---|---|---|
| A game minimizing itself when Cheat Engine takes the foreground | One older title, reproducibly | Two current titles; one of them was confirmed here starting alongside Cheat Engine without going dark. The restore path is exercised by older titles, and a newer game proves nothing about it either way |
| The restore capability itself | Confirmed on a second Proton (GE-Proton11-2) and a second prefix, with a 142-record table: `restore_capability=ready`, `minimized_query=IsIconic` | Not specific to the one game or the one Proton it was found on |
| An empty Cheat Engine symbol table | Inside a game's own Wine session | A plugin-owned prefix of its own, where every symbol resolves |
| A one-pixel `window.innerHeight` | Every screen this plugin draws, on both machines: its code runs in `SharedJSContext` | The pages the DOM is in, which report their real size to a node that is in them |

## 4. Table sources evaluated

The blocker is almost never the transport. Of the sources examined, one is blocked by a WAF that contradicts its own robots policy, one gates the file behind an account, one disallows the attachment route in robots, and the ones that work do so because the operator publishes a sitemap or an API and permits the routes involved.

| Source | Decision | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| FearLess Revolution | In use | Its own search route challenges anonymous HTTP, so discovery is a bounded local index of the readable listing rather than a search |
| Playground | In use | The game's own table category is the only listing fetched, because the same section also holds trainers, saves, save editors and fixes, and filenames cannot separate them |
| GitHub | In use | Repository index only: code search answers HTTP 401 unauthenticated, so a table cannot be found by file extension. An anonymous client gets 10 search requests per minute and 60 core requests per hour, per client IP, measured 2026-09-02. A release asset carries `digest: "sha256:..."`; a file committed in a tree carries git's own object name, which is verified rather than accepted and never presented as a content digest |
| The Cheat Script | In use | Only the sitemap its `robots.txt` declares is followed; search, category, tag and feed routes are disallowed and never requested |
| VGTimes | In use | The chain is read from the site's own lazy-loaded bundle at run time rather than frozen into the adapter, so the day it moves the adapter reports that it no longer understands the contract instead of sending a confident wrong answer |
| Open Cheat Tables | Rejected | A site-wide Cloudflare challenge, not a per-path rule. Measured 2026-09-02 with the production network client: HTTP 403 and the challenge interstitial on `/`, `viewtopic.php`, `viewforum.php`, `download/file.php`, `?view=print`, `feed.php`, `app.php/feed/*`, `index.php`, and even `favicon.ico` and a static stylesheet, on both domains. Only `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` answer 200, and both are edge served. Request shape is not the discriminator: an honest agent, the same agent with standard `Accept` headers, and one carrying a contact URL were challenged identically, because the interstitial requires JavaScript. The site's own robots permits exactly the topic routes it will not serve |
| Web archive as a fallback for the above | Parked, not adopted | It works and circumvents no access control, because the archive is a separate consenting service: verified end to end 2026-09-02, an archived attachment returned 413,501 bytes of a valid table. What it costs: 707 of 1,582 topic IDs are archived, so roughly half the catalog is absent; the archive advertises no publisher digest, so provenance degrades to a snapshot timestamp; and the load lands on a nonprofit. One alternative archive does not answer automation and another no longer resolves, so there is no second option |
| UnknownCheats | Rejected | Transport and metadata are good and anonymous, including a published SHA-256 per file, but the download action answers HTTP 403 without a registered account and this plugin has no account model and must not acquire one. A metadata-only source is worse than none, because the panel may present only what it can download itself. The operator's robots also disallows the downloads path |
| `bbs.3dmgame.com` | Rejected | Answers anonymously with no challenge, but its `robots.txt` disallows `/*?mod=attachment*`, which is exactly the URL shape its forum software serves attachments through. Browsing is permitted and downloading is not |
| `bbs.ali213.net` | Not evaluated | Did not resolve or connect from this device |

| Real table corpus | `atul1503/Cheat-Engine-Tables@893a25cc`, `FreeER/CE-Examples@04ec4e91`, `Hexorg/CheatEngineTables@0e7092b2` | Public tables covering flat scalar records, non-sequential IDs, nested group hierarchies, Auto Assembler with embedded Lua, static dropdowns, alias-expanded dropdown text, and a script that creates roughly 300 records at run time |

## 7. Decisions taken once, and the reason

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Use the native Linux Cheat Engine as the runtime? | No. Upstream itself expects Windows Cheat Engine inside the target Proton environment: its own Linux build's `protonlauncher.lua` copies a Windows installation into `windowsbin` and launches that. Ordinary table compatibility follows the Windows build |
| Use the official Cheat Engine Proton launcher? | Reference only. It corroborates game, compatdata and Proton selection; it is not an architecture dependency |
| Build custom `protonhax` or `wineserver` orchestration? | No. An exact installed Proton tool and an owned process group answer the same need without inventing a launcher |
| Bundle a 7-Zip binary? | No. The host tool is discovered once and used by absolute path, and a device whose build lacks a format's handler drops those rows at search rather than after a download |
| Treat a visible Cheat Engine window as a successful launch? | No. The resident bridge's heartbeat for that exact session is the only success signal; a mapped window is in fact a failure mode, because it takes the game's audio and controller with it |
| Replace a table inside a running Cheat Engine with `loadTable(stream, false, true)`? | No. Public Cheat Engine source maps that third flag to trainer-mode `LoadXML` behaviour: it executes the table's Lua without prompting, which is the exact consent boundary this product exists to hold, and a Lua error there can terminate Cheat Engine. In-process replacement stays post-v1 for its own reasons; this particular shortcut would not be the way to reach it |
| Check the Decky Store's generative-AI attestation to make a submission eligible? | No, and the submission is made without it. The checklist asks the submitter to state that generative AI did not write a majority of the submitted code, and this project cannot state that: `README.md` **Credits** names the models that assisted, and the contract refuses both an inaccurate attestation and scrubbing honest provenance to satisfy a checkbox. The store's own automation does not enforce it, so a submission with the box unchecked is accepted by the description bot and reaches human review; what the one recorded case of a maintainer reaching an unchecked box says is that it is treated as a required item, and that pull request was closed the day the submitter explained why it was unchecked. Read on 2026-09-14 across every open plugin addition and the last hundred closed pull requests of `decky-plugin-database`: no addition created after 2026-04-02 had been merged, the attestation entered the template on 2026-04-10, and additions that died did so from the stale-review automation for want of a third-party tester rather than from the attestation. So the expected outcome of the submission is refusal, the decision is to make it anyway and let the policy be the thing that refuses it, and public GitHub releases are the distribution route that does not depend on it |
| Identify Cheat Engine compatibility by version string? | No. The identity is the exact executable SHA-256, the complete source-tree SHA-256, the bridge SHA-256 and the exact Proton identity |

The 0.9.22 foreground request uses public Cheat Engine `ec45d5f4` `LuaHandler.pas` (`executeCodeLocalEx`, `lua_getForegroundWindow`) and Microsoft's `SetForegroundWindow` API contract as behavioral evidence only; no upstream code was copied or adapted. The pinned tree has no top-level license file; it was used only as API evidence, not as a source-reuse dependency. The API may refuse the request; only readback counts as foreground success. The older bridge comment rejecting SetForegroundWindow merely because CE calls it was an untested rationale, replaced by an exact-target request with bounded refusal diagnostics. This does not replace the measured need for `SC_RESTORE` on iconic windows or the application notification established on the older title.

The read-only Steam build reader also checked `ark120202/find-steam-app@1b33b5d9de5967f29cb7ceae9af85a8d15384d29`, `src/manifest.ts` and its MIT `LICENSE`, for the per-AppID manifest filename and `buildid` field. Behavioral evidence only; no code was copied or adapted. CE Decky keeps its stricter bounded reads, exact AppState AppID check and ambiguity refusal.

```

`docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`:

```md
# Improvements

Changes that would make CE Decky better and that nothing owes. The product is correct without each of them: what the device does today is stated in `DESIGN.md` and is true, and a row here is a better answer to a case that already has a safe one.

This list is not `FIELD_NOTES.md` **Still worth checking**. That section holds what this project has not confirmed, and `scripts/check_release.py` refuses a stable tag while it holds a row. Nothing here holds a release. A row moves there only when what the product does today in its case turns out to be wrong rather than merely limited, and a row is deleted here in the change that builds it.

Each row names what already exists, so the next person starts from it rather than from the idea, and what has to be true before the improvement reaches a user.

| Improvement | What exists | What it needs before it is offered |
|---|---|---|
| A cheat that cannot be switched off safely is taken out of the prepared copy, rather than reported and left on | The transform is written: the hook belongs to a scan symbol, and dropping that symbol removes it with both existing proofs. Measured at 5 blocks, 90 lines and 2264 bytes on the table this was found in | The cost report counts a record whose address the removal took and a script the removal emptied; a record whose flag no longer has any reader is neither, so such a cheat would go quietly and has to be counted. `prepare_table_copy` carries it as a third transform beside the signature and the unmatched scans, in the same press and the same copy. And a game that dies seconds after CE Decky wrote anything is the only signal for the shapes the reader cannot follow: correlating the game's own exit with the write is what would turn those into something the user is told about rather than left to guess |
| A flag whose hook changes a register only on its on side is proven safe to switch off, rather than left on | The hook reader refuses any register load, push or pop on either side of a flag's test, because it does not know which side runs when the flag is off. On the table the crash came from that refuses three flags whose off side is the original code (14 of 22 safe rather than 17), and 44 of 67 over the 12 tables on the Steam Machine rather than 51 | The side that runs when the flag is off, read from the record's own off key against the test's literal and the branch's condition, for `je`/`jne` and their aliases at least, with every other condition still attributed to both sides. Each test of the flag decided separately, since a hook may test it more than once. A flag with no record, or whose record has no off key, keeps today's answer. The reader's one-direction rule holds throughout: a shape the direction cannot be read for stays refused |

```

```md
# Documentation

The documents in this directory have distinct roles. Keep a fact in the narrowest authoritative document instead of copying it into several files.

| Document | Purpose |
|---|---|

| [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) | Production components, data flow, and system boundaries |

`FIELD_NOTES.md` is also read by `scripts/check_release.py`: while its **Still worth checking** section holds a row, a stable release tag is refused. Removing the last row is what permits one, so keep that section true: an improvement that is not owed goes to `IMPROVEMENTS.md`, which no gate reads.
```
